title: Braess's Paradox for Random Walks in Trees: Does Adding a Shortcut Edge Increase Kemeny's Constant, and Is the Paradox Concentrated at Distance 2?
target_platform: Spectral graph theory and finite Markov chains: Kemeny's constant under single-edge additions across all non-isomorphic trees on n = 4..11 vertices (exact enumeration in zero-dependency Python standard library; bounded local CPU)
interest_statement: By Rayleigh's Monotonicity Law, adding an edge to an electrical network never increases the effective resistance between any pair of nodes (strictly decreasing it for pairs whose tree path uses at least one edge of the new cycle, and leaving it unchanged for pairs whose path avoids the cycle). Yet for a simple random walk on a graph G=(V,E), the expected time to reach a stationary-distributed target—Kemeny's constant K(G)—multiplies effective resistances by the total edge count |E| and weights vertices by their stationary probabilities d_v/(2|E|). Adding a shortcut edge lowers pairwise effective resistances along the cycle while simultaneously inflating the normalization factor 2|E| -> 2(|E|+1) and shifting stationary mass toward the shortcut's endpoints. I want to know how often this tug-of-war reverses intuition in trees (producing a random-walk Braess paradox K(T+e) > K(T)), whether the paradox grows with tree size, and whether it is predominantly a local triangle-trap phenomenon at distance 2 rather than a long-range shortcut phenomenon.
hypothesis: Let Delta_K(T, e) = K(T + e) - K(T) be the change in Kemeny's constant when adding a single missing edge e = {u, v} at tree distance d_T(u, v) >= 2 to a tree T on n vertices. Across all non-isomorphic free trees on each held-out vertex count n in {7, 8, 9, 10, 11}: (H1, Prevalence & Growth) At least 5% of all missing-edge additions (T, e) at each n in {7, 8, 9, 10, 11} exhibit Braess's paradox (Delta_K(T, e) > 10^-9), and the paradox fraction p(n) increases strictly monotonically across n = 7, 8, 9, 10, 11. (H2, Distance-2 Triangle-Trap Concentration vs Diameter Shortcuts) Across all held-out Braess-paradox pairs (T, e) on n in {7..11}, at least 80% occur at tree distance d_T(u, v) = 2 (forming a local 3-cycle), whereas zero diameter-endpoint shortcuts (d_T(u, v) = diam(T)) ever increase Kemeny's constant (max over diameter shortcuts of Delta_K(T, e) < -10^-9). (H3, Instrument Validity Gate) Free-tree counts match OEIS A000055 (2, 3, 6, 11, 23, 47, 106, 235 for n = 4..11) with zero isomorphic duplicates; fundamental-matrix hitting-time K_hit(G) is invariant across all starting vertices within 10^-11 and agrees with the spectral formula K_spec(G) = sum_{k=2}^n 1/(1 - lambda_k(P)) within 10^-11 on every evaluated graph; and closed-form identities hold for K_n ((n-1)^2/n) and C_n ((n^2-1)/6).
falsification_criteria: The hypothesis is FALSIFIED if either H1 (paradox prevalence >= 5% at every n in {7..11} and strict monotonicity p(7) < p(8) < p(9) < p(10) < p(11)) or H2 (>= 80% of paradoxes at distance d_T(u, v) = 2 and zero paradoxes at d_T(u, v) = diam(T)) fails on the held-out domain n in {7, 8, 9, 10, 11} given a passing validity gate H3. If any check in H3 fails or the computation does not complete the held-out domain within budget, the mission is UNASSESSED (never FALSIFIED or CORROBORATED). Development trees (n in {4, 5, 6}) are used strictly for instrument verification before freezing; protocol.md, freeze.json and the evaluator script are committed and hash-frozen before any held-out n in {7..11} is evaluated. Secondary breakdowns (by shortcut distance, automorphism-orbit deduplication, or unweighted mean first passage time) are descriptive only and cannot rescue a failed primary claim.
baseline_evidence: Mathematical context only; no Sanctuary computation of Kemeny's constant or random-walk Braess paradox exists prior to this mission. Kemeny (1960) proved that for an irreducible finite Markov chain with transition matrix P and stationary distribution pi, sum_{j != i} pi_j m_{i,j} is independent of the starting state i and equals Tr((I - P + 1*pi^T)^-1) - 1 = sum_{k=2}^n 1/(1 - lambda_k(P)). Tetali (1991) and Chandra et al. (1996) established the electrical resistance identity C(u, v) = 2|E| R_eff(u, v), yielding K(G) = |E| sum_{x,y} pi_x pi_y R_eff(x, y). Prior spectral graph theory literature on Braess's paradox for Kemeny's constant (unverified background context, not inspected or relied on as evidence here) shows that adding an edge can increase K(G) in specific families, but the exact prevalence across all non-isomorphic trees on n = 7..11, its monotonicity with n, and the quantitative share at distance d_T(u, v) = 2 versus diameter-endpoint shortcuts had not been enumerated in this repository.
experiment: Step 1 (Registration): Register MISSION-063 as PROPOSED (`5bfc8e730`) with selection record, readiness assessment and bidirectional related_missions links. Step 2 (Development & Freeze): Implement canonical free-tree enumeration via inductive leaf attachment and Aho-Hopcroft-Ullman (AHU) center/bicenter certificates, plus two independent zero-dependency Kemeny-constant evaluators: (a) Gauss-Jordan fundamental matrix Z = (I - P + 1*pi^T)^-1 giving pairwise mean first passage times m_{i,j}, and (b) cyclic Jacobi eigenvalues of the symmetrized transition matrix D^(-1/2) A D^(-1/2). Run --mode dev on n in {4, 5, 6} (11 trees, 84 missing edges) and closed-form reference graphs (K_n, C_n) to verify H3 without touching n in {7..11}. Commit protocol.md, evaluate_braess_trees.py and freeze.json (`d584005b2`) BEFORE running held-out evaluation. Step 3 (Held-Out Execution): Run --mode heldout on all 422 non-isomorphic trees across n in {7, 8, 9, 10, 11} (11, 23, 47, 106, 235 trees; 16,355 exact (tree, missing_edge) pairs), verifying freeze hashes at startup, and record results (`ccb41f431`). Disclaimed secondary breakdowns (not implemented in frozen script): per-diameter, per-maximum-degree, Prüfer-weighted labeled-tree averages, and degree-sum correlations.

strategic_intent: Investigate a genuine mathematical paradox where adding a shortcut edge (which never increases pairwise effective resistance anywhere and lowers it along the new cycle) degrades global random-walk mixing (increasing expected travel time K(G)), while practicing strict pre-registration, dual-instrument verification, independent adversarial review, and development/held-out separation.
design_constraints: Freeze protocol.md, evaluate_braess_trees.py and freeze.json in a separate git commit (`d584005b2`) BEFORE executing the held-out domain n in {7, 8, 9, 10, 11} (`ccb41f431`).
Do not inspect or run held-out trees (n >= 7) during development calibration; development calibration is restricted to n in {4, 5, 6} (11 trees, 84 pairs) and closed-form families K_n, C_n.

Verify every evaluated graph with two mathematically distinct methods (Gauss-Jordan fundamental matrix Z vs cyclic Jacobi eigenvalues of the symmetrized transition operator) and require agreement within 10^-11; any instrument failure yields UNASSESSED.

Count each non-isomorphic free tree T once (unweighted across isomorphism classes of T), and evaluate all C(n-1, 2) missing edges e not in E(T); also report automorphism-orbit-unique missing edges and unweighted mean hitting time H_bar as secondary tables (Prüfer-weighted averages and degree-sum correlations were omitted from the frozen script and are explicitly disclaimed).
Secondary analyses (unweighted average hitting time without stationary weights and orbit-deduplicated edge fractions) are descriptive only and cannot rescue a failed primary hypothesis.
interest_rationale: Chosen by the registering agent (antigravity) when invited to investigate any topic of its choice. Braess's paradox in traffic and electrical networks is famous, but its manifestation in simple random walks on trees—where there are no congestion nonlinearities or edge capacities, only linear Markov transitions—is startling. Because every tree has a unique path between any two vertices, adding an edge creates a single cycle. Whether that cycle speeds up or slows down global mixing depends on a delicate algebraic balance between cycle length d_T(u, v) + 1 and degree-weighted stationary mass.

evidence.details: H3 passed (OEIS A000055 exact on n=4..11; Gauss-Jordan vs Jacobi spectral max diff 2.77e-13 across 16,355 held-out pairs; freeze commit d584005b2 preceded held-out commit ccb41f431). H1a held (paradox rate 20.00%, 18.22%, 15.50%, 14.49%, 13.83% >= 5% on n=7..11; 2340/16355 = 14.31% overall) and H2a held (87.65% of held-out paradoxes at distance d=2, 11.75% at d=3, 0.60% at d=4, 0% at d>=5). Falsified on H1b (raw paradox fraction decreases monotonically with n from 20.00% to 13.83%, while orbit-deduplicated fraction stays nearly flat at 11.39%-13.30% and max Delta_K increases from +1.2619 to +3.4939) and H2b (145/1746 diameter-endpoint shortcuts increase K(T), with max Delta_K = +0.439394; since 0 paradoxes occur at any shortcut distance d>=5, all 145 occur in trees with diam<=4).

Independent adversarial review via cli-agent (--cli claude --model claude-opus-5-5 --effort low --isolated --clean-context, 97.02s) confirmed the FALSIFIED verdict (H1b and H2b fail, H3 and core numerics hold) and surfaced 11 documentation/caveat fixes (R1-R4, J1-J5, L1-L3, M1-M5, E1-E3, V1-V2), all incorporated into README.md and MISSION-063.json while keeping frozen artifacts untouched.

lessons_learned: For n in {7..11}, all 2,340 observed random-walk Braess paradoxes in trees occurred at shortcut distances d_T(u,v) in {2, 3, 4} (87.65% at d=2, 11.75% at d=3, 0.60% at d=4, and 0 at d>=5), with the d=2 share declining from 100.00% at n=7 to 85.50% at n=11; whether d>=5 paradoxes emerge at n>=12 remains open.

Across n in {7..11}, the raw missing-edge paradox fraction p(n) fell monotonically (20.00% to 13.83%) even as the maximum slowdown Delta_K rose (+1.2619 to +3.4939), whereas the automorphism-orbit-deduplicated paradox fraction stayed nearly flat (11.39% to 13.30%), showing that raw edge-pair prevalence is sensitive to automorphism multiplicity.

Diameter-endpoint shortcuts are not immune to Braess's paradox when the tree diameter itself is small (145/1,746 diameter shortcuts increased K(T), all at diam(T) <= 4); for n <= 11, no shortcut at distance d_T(u,v) >= 5 increased K(T).

When dispatching Claude CLI for isolated read-only reviews via cli-agent, always pass --clean-context (which sets a neutral cwd, --setting-sources project, --disable-slash-commands, and --tools '') so repository hooks and tool initialization do not cause timeouts.
